title: uslecn-abm-erosion v1.2.2 — NetLogo implementation of a runoff-weighted LS factor (LS_CN), paired simulation outputs and R analysis code
description:
NetLogo 7.0.2 implementation of LS_CN, a topographic index in which SCS-CN event runoff ratios weight the specific contributing area before the RUSLE slope-length exponent, together with the complete paired simulation outputs and the R analysis code behind the manuscript by Bednář and Šarapatka on a runoff-weighted contributing-area index for analysing landscape-configuration effects on erosion potential in strip-cropped agriculture.

What this archive contains

  • netlogo/usle_abm_model_LE_LFIX.nlogo — the model version that produced every run in this archive. It contains the corrected flow-accumulation expression: the contributing area is raised to the slope-length exponent as a whole, and the runoff ratio multiplies the contributing area rather than the slope length. The SCS-CN denominator is P + 0.8 S, consistent with Ia = 0.2 S.
  • data/outputs/raw/ — 33 BehaviorSpace output tables (CP1250, seven-line header) covering 14 experiment families.
  • data/outputs/derived/pairs.csv — 8,730 paired scenarios, each giving the classical-LS and the LS_CN result for the same factor combination, with all design factors.
  • data/outputs/derived/coverage.csv — per-file completeness check; the maximum imbalance statistic is 0 for all 33 files.
  • analysis/R/ — the scripts that build the paired table and reproduce Tables 1 and 2 of the manuscript.
  • data/landuse/, data/realblocks/, data/virtual_blocks/ — the C-factor strip patterns, the real-DEM-derived terrain templates and the synthetic terrain blocks.
  • docs/ — ODD protocol, two technical supplements and the console logs of the analysis.

Simulation design: 120 × 120 cells of 5 × 5 m, multiple-flow-direction routing, full factorial over crop order, division type, strip length, strip angle, rainfall depth, terrain morphology, flow pattern and soil region. Each scenario was run twice — once with classical LS and once with LS_CN — with every other input identical.

Verified reproduction: the pairing script regenerates pairs.csv byte-identically from data/outputs/raw/, and the two table scripts reproduce the published coefficients exactly (Table 1: n = 7,200, R2 = 0.262, AIC = 42,351.0; Table 2: n = 14,400 rows, deviance explained 57.8 %, AIC = 78,631.8, method coefficient -4.674).

Changes in v1.2.0: corrected L-factor exponentiation in the model (the previous expression applied the exponent to the denominator only, so L grew linearly with flow accumulation) and a consistent SCS-CN denominator; the complete paired output tables and the analysis code are added; the two terrain rasters that were truncated in earlier versions are restored and the missing ce4.asc is added; claims in the README that were not supported by the archived data have been removed.

Scope and limitations: these are model outputs only. No measured runoff, soil loss or sediment yield is included, no observational validation is claimed, and the model performs no sediment routing or deposition. Real-DEM scenarios use DMR 4G derivatives as terrain templates and are not field plots. All comparisons are model-to-model, under a defined homogeneous counterfactual.

Licensing: code under MIT (see LICENSE); data and documentation under CC BY 4.0.

Requirements: NetLogo 7.0.2 for the model, R 4.4 with dplyr and mgcv for the analysis, Python 3.8+ for the terrain and land-use generators.
